analysis.investment_thesis: Emami is a genuinely excellent consumer business — ROCE of 32.4% and operating margins of 29.4% are top-decile — but at an earnings yield of only ~5.1% (EBIT INR 1,014 Cr / EV ~INR 19,721 Cr), the Magic Formula won't pull the trigger here. One leg of the formula is outstanding; the other is below the minimum threshold.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE 32.4% sustained, ROE 30.2% — exactly the kind of durable moat Magic Formula loves
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.02, debt INR 90 Cr) with strong FCF conversion — OCF INR 896 Cr vs Net Profit INR 803 Cr in FY25
Diversified branded portfolio (BoroPlus, Navratna, Zandu, Kesh King) with pricing power evident in 29.4% operating margins and 68% gross margins
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 5.5% over 9 years is sluggish for a consumer brand — the Magic Formula requires quality AND growth to justify a premium
Earnings yield ~5.1% (EBIT/EV) is below the 6% floor Greenblatt requires; EV/EBITDA of 19.4x and P/E of 24.6x offer little margin of safety
EBITDA growth has been nearly flat (1.1% CAGR over 9 years) — operating leverage isn't materializing at the bottom line despite margin strength
red_flags: Earnings yield of 5.1% falls below Greenblatt's minimum attractive threshold of 6% — the stock is priced for perfection
EBITDA contracted in the 5-year trend despite revenue expanding — a divergence that warrants scrutiny on cost structure
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Emami: EBIT FY25 = INR 1,014 Cr; Enterprise Value = Market Cap INR 19,736 Cr + Debt INR 90 Cr − Cash INR 105 Cr = ~INR 19,721 Cr. **Earnings Yield = 5.1%** — below the 6% floor, meaning the market is not offering a bargain. On the other leg, **ROCE of 32.4%** is genuinely excellent and sustained, confirming this is a high-quality business with real competitive advantages in ayurvedic/personal care branding. The two Formula scores are wildly asymmetric: top-quintile quality, bottom-quintile cheapness.

The business fundamentals are sound — almost pristine. Debt is negligible, free cash flow of INR 852 Cr exceeds net profit, and promoter holding at 54.8% aligns interests. But volume growth at 5.5% revenue CAGR over nine years signals that Emami is a mature, slow-growth franchise, not a compounder accelerating into a large TAM. At P/E 24.6x and EV/EBITDA 19.4x, you're paying a full price for a steady, high-quality business — exactly what Greenblatt's formula says to avoid until valuation corrects. Watch for a 20–25% price decline that pushes earnings yield above 7–8% before initiating a position.
